decisions.summary: A* KEPT: 2.4% faster in all against a 0.6% same-run spread
decisions.why: FR-001 as written. Re-derived from astarcmp/results.json: A* 207.07 s against 211.53 and 212.74 s, 442 households seated, 29 connectors. Its first-attempt strandings (8 against 6) are healed by re-roll; SC-011 counts seated houses, and FR-003's every-attempt rule is the lattice's alone.

decisions.summary: the coarser lattice withdrawn: 12 px strands two maps the 10 px lattice did not
decisions.why: The same defect as round 1, the other way round. b2/harness.py swaps nothing and ran on the tree as it stood at 20:27, with A* and FR-004 both withdrawn. Its 10 px row (5 unreached over every attempt, 2 re-rolls) is exactly combined/results.json's 'levers off' pass; the shipping engine at 10 px is 8 unreached and 6 re-rolls. A* and FR-004 were re-instated at 5afcaea81, so B2 was measured on a router and field search that do not ship. R4 labels it 'on the engine that ships', which is false. Round 1's own reasoning applies: the router and the field decide which maps strand (R6) and strandings move chaotically with the cell (R4), so a comparison with both levers off says nothing about the cell on the engine that ships. That goes for the strandings and for the 'slower at every cell' timings too, since those come from re-rolls. Re-run b2/harness.py on the engine as it ships (A*, FR-004, FR-014, the connector fix) and take or withdraw the cell by that. Then correct R4, the ROUTE_CELL docstring (which still says '20 unreached ... against 8, and cohort seed 03 kept a stranded house', figures no current run shows) and the spec's Amendment 1 FR-003 bullet (the same stale figures, and 'Measured with A* in the router ... before FR-001 was withdrawn').
